Seoul, South Korea —
Patrick Finn, a 95-year-old Korean War veteran, watches from a wheelchair as a staff member uses a pencil to rub the name “Edmund Hubert Reilly” from the Wall of the Fallen onto a piece of paper.
US military archives call the Korean War “The Forgotten War,” though some 1.8 million Americans served during its three years – and more than 36,500 of them died, along with at least 200,000 South Korean, 400,000 North Korean and 600,000 Chinese troops.
But Finn, who fought in one of the war’s bloodiest battles, has never forgotten the Marine from Center Point, Iowa, who saved his life twice. He will carry his name back home to Minnesota.

Who is Alice Huang, the woman allegedly at the center of the scandal enveloping the world’s most powerful chip company?
She’s been photographed with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (no relation) at banquet dinners and golf resorts, clinking wine glasses and even leaving an event with him in the same car.
But for someone suddenly generating international headlines, she remains something of a mystery.
Her limited online footprint paints a picture of a journalist-turned tech power broker who held senior positions at financial firms in Asia.
